counterfactual_missing_items: diffuse ST-segment elevation or PR depression on ECG
decisive_items: Subsequent cardiac windows revealed a small pericardial effusion.
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete supported composite because it explicitly includes the small pericardial effusion found on ultrasound, directly matching the acute presentation. R1 shares the same core pericarditis evidence but omits the complication, so it is only slightly less complete. R2 and C2 rely on chronic hypertension/LVH and do not account for the acute pericardial effusion. Generator opinions were disregarded; only raw spans and label completeness were used.

rejected.why: Hypertensive heart disease does not explain the acute small pericardial effusion or acute epigastric pain; hypertension and LVH are background findings.
Adding left ventricular hypertrophy to hypertensive heart disease still fails to explain the decisive acute finding of a small pericardial effusion.
